mainTopic: The טומאה of עבודה זרה (היסט, broken pieces, minimum size, rabbinic leniency), and why a ship cannot become טמא, with lessons on devotion to Torah study
overview: This amud first finishes the discussion of how עבודה זרה makes things טמא. The גמרא shows that a ברייתא about the היסט of a זב can still fit רבי עקיבא, because 'זב' includes everything like it. רב חמא בר גוריא asks whether broken pieces of an idol carry טומאה, and the question stays unresolved (תיקו). רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks about an idol smaller than a כזית. After רב יוסף shows that tiny idols are clearly forbidden, the question is narrowed to טומאה, and a ברייתא rules that less than a כזית has no טומאה, like a מת. According to רבנן, the טומאה of idols is only דרבנן, so its comparisons to שרץ, נדה, and מת teach only leniencies. Next comes a new משנה: a ship cannot become טמא, learned from 'דרך אניה בלב ים'. חנניה learns the same law from a שק instead, and the גמרא shows the two sources differ about an earthenware ship and a Jordan River boat. The amud ends with lessons about never leaving the בית המדרש and devoting oneself fully to Torah, and רבא's statement begins at the very end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the scale case: the food stays pure
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a ברייתא from the previous section: if the food's side of the scale went down, the food stays טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they (the food and drink) tipped the scale, they are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the final words of a ברייתא that started on the previous amud. It is about a scale with a source of טומאה on one side and food on the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the food is heavier and pulls its own side down, the source of טומאה did not move the food. So no היסט happened, and the food stays טהור. This sets up the next question about which kinds of טומאה can make things טמא through moving.

keyTerms.meaning: they tipped / bent down (the scale went down on their side)

phrases.english: If they tipped (the scale), they are pure.
phrases.notes: Tail end of a ברייתא begun on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the food's own weight tips the scale, it was not moved by the טומאה and stays טהור.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא that only a זב makes things impure by moving them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying only a זב makes things טמא by moving them. It suggests this ברייתא cannot match רבי עקיבא, because he holds עבודה זרה does this too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this ברייתא follow: 'All impure things that move objects leave them pure, except the moving done by a זב, which has no counterpart in the entire Torah'? Let us say it does not follow רבי עקיבא. If it followed רבי עקיבא, there would also be עבודה זרה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says only a זב can make something טמא just by moving it. It suggests this ברייתא must disagree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that עבודה זרה makes things טמא the way a נדה does, and that includes moving. So the ברייתא's claim that the זב is the only one 'with no counterpart' seems to leave out עבודה זרה. That suggests the ברייתא was not written by רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: according to whom does it go? (whose view is this?)
moving something; a way of passing on טומאה without touching or carrying
a man with a certain bodily discharge who is a major source of טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'הטומאות המסיטות טהורות' does not mean the sources of טומאה are pure. It means that the objects they move stay pure.

phrases.english: According to whom is that which was taught (in a baraita):
All impure things that move (objects) — (the objects remain) pure,
except for the moving done by a zav,
for which we have not found a counterpart
in the entire Torah —
shall we say it is not according to Rabbi Akiva?
For if it were according to Rabbi Akiva —
there is also idolatry!
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא holds that idolatry passes on טומאה like a נדה, including by moving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי עקיבא's view, from the previous discussion, against a different ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the ברייתא about היסט of a זב match רבי עקיבא's view?
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the ברייתא fits רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the זב is unique, but according to רבי עקיבא, עבודה זרה would also make things טמא through moving.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a זב and anything like it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא can fit רבי עקיבא, because 'זב' there includes everything similar to a זב, such as עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי עקיבא: the ברייתא taught 'a זב and anything like it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא can follow רבי עקיבא after all. The word 'זב' stands for a whole group, not just one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, עבודה זרה is compared to a נדה, and a נדה is in the same group as a זב. So when the ברייתא names the זב, it means everything treated like a זב. There is no contradiction with רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: you can even say (introduces a defense)
and everything that is similar to it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, עבודה זרה belongs to the 'זב group' and makes things טמא even by moving them (היסט).

phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabbi Akiva:
(the baraita) taught 'zav' and everything similar to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא more broadly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זב' means only a זב, so the ברייתא would exclude עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זב' stands for the zav and everything like it, which includes עבודה זרה according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Do broken pieces of an idol still carry impurity?
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר גוריא asks whether עבודה זרה makes things טמא even when it is in pieces (אברים).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר גוריא asked: Does עבודה זרה make things impure in its separate pieces, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב חמא בר גוריא asks whether broken parts of an idol still have the טומאה of עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the idol is in pieces, maybe it no longer counts as an idol. Or maybe each piece still counts. The next steps narrow down exactly which case is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked (a real question that needs an answer)

phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Guria asked:
Does idolatry (impart impurity) in its limbs,
or not in its limbs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the טומאה of עבודה זרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether pieces of an idol keep its טומאה.

steps.title: First version: the doubt is only when an ordinary person cannot reassemble it
steps.stepSummary: If an ordinary person can put the idol back together, it obviously still counts as whole. The doubt is only when an ordinary person cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where an ordinary person can put it back together, there is no question: it is like it is attached. The question is where an ordinary person cannot put it back together. What then? Since an ordinary person cannot fix it, is it like it is broken? Or perhaps, since no piece is missing, it still counts as whole?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רב חמא's question. It explains which case is clear and which case is really in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an ordinary person can reassemble the idol, it is treated as still attached, so it keeps its טומאה. If only an expert could fix it, maybe it counts as broken. On the other hand, nothing is actually missing, so maybe it still counts as a whole idol.

keyTerms.meaning: don't ask this; it is obvious
or perhaps (introduces the other side of a doubt)

phrases.english: Where an ordinary person can put it back together —
do not ask,
for it is like it is attached.
Where you should ask

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּאֵין הֶדְיוֹט יָכוֹל לְהַחֲזִירָהּ, מַאי?
phrases.english: is where an ordinary person cannot put it back together — what (is the law)?
Since an ordinary person cannot put it back together —
is it like it is broken?
Or perhaps, it is not missing anything?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּהֶדְיוֹט יָכוֹל לְהַחֲזִירָהּ לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines exactly which case רב חמא was asking about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an idol that only an expert can reassemble count as broken, or as whole because nothing is missing?

steps.title: Second version: the doubt is only when an ordinary person can reassemble it
steps.stepSummary: Others reverse it. If an ordinary person cannot fix the idol, it is clearly broken. The doubt is when an ordinary person can fix it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some ask the question the other way: Where an ordinary person cannot put it back together, there is no question: it is like it is broken. The question is where an ordinary person can put it back together. What then? Since an ordinary person can fix it, is it like it is attached? Or perhaps, right now at least, it is pulled apart and lying in pieces?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same question. It flips which case is obvious and which case is in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, an idol that only an expert can fix is clearly broken and has no טומאה. The doubt is about an idol an ordinary person can fix. Do we look at how easily it can be fixed, or at the fact that right now it is in pieces?

phrases.english: And some ask it in the other direction:
Where an ordinary person cannot put it back together —

phrases.aramaic: לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, דִּכְמַאן דְּמִתַּבְרָא דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: do not ask, for it is like it is broken;
where you should ask
is where an ordinary person can put it back together — what (is the law)?
Since an ordinary person can put it back together —
is it like it is attached?
Or perhaps, right now at least,
it is pulled apart and lying (in pieces)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reversed version of the question in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an idol that an ordinary person can reassemble count as whole, or as broken because it is in pieces right now?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found for either version, so the question is left standing (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends רב חמא's question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither version of the question gets resolved. 'תיקו' means the question remains open.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand; the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Whether broken pieces of an idol carry טומאה is left unresolved (תיקו), in both versions of the question.

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes both versions of the question.

steps.title: What is the law for an idol smaller than an olive?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks about an idol smaller than a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asked: What is the law for an idol that is smaller than an olive-bulk?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins, about a very small idol, less than the size of an olive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question does not yet say which law it is asking about. That gap is what רב יוסף points out next.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami asked:
Idolatry less than an olive-bulk — what is (the law)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about עבודה זרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law of an idol smaller than a כזית.

steps.title: A tiny idol is obviously still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects: if the question is about the איסור, the answer is obvious, since even a fly-sized idol like זבוב בעל עקרון was worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: About what? If you say it is about the prohibition, it is no different from זבוב בעל עקרון!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges the question. He shows that it cannot be about whether a small idol is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זבוב בעל עקרון was a tiny, fly-sized idol, and it was still a real idol. So size does not matter for the איסור of עבודה זרה. The question must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: a fly-shaped idol, the god of the city עקרון

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected: For what (law)?
If you say regarding the prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהֵא אֶלָּא זְבוּב בַּעַל עֶקְרוֹן.
phrases.english: let it be no worse than Zevuv, the Baal of Ekron!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scope of the question in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: Asking about the איסור of a small idol
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tiny idols like זבוב בעל עקרון were clearly worshipped, so size does not matter for the איסור.

steps.title: Proof: people kept tiny idols in their pockets
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that people worshipped tiny pocket-sized idols, so small idols are clearly forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And they made בעל ברית their god' — this is זבוב בעל עקרון. This teaches that each person made a likeness of his god and kept it in his pocket. Whenever he remembered it, he took it out, hugged it, and kissed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב יוסף's point with a ברייתא about tiny idols kept in a pocket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An idol small enough to fit in a pocket was still worshipped. This proves that size does not affect the איסור of עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Baal Berit, an idol mentioned in שופטים
an image of what he worships

phrases.english: As it was taught:
"And they made Baal Berit their god" (Judges 8:33) —
this is Zevuv, the Baal of Ekron.
This teaches that each and every one
would make an image of his god
and place it in his pocket;
whenever he remembered it, he would take it out of his pocket
and hug it and kiss it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא וַיָּשִׂימוּ לָהֶם בַּעַל בְּרִית לֶאֱלֹהִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's objection.
steps.raayaObject: That a tiny idol is still forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on שופטים ח:לג about pocket idols

steps.title: The real question is about impurity: lentil-size or olive-size?
steps.stepSummary: The question must be about טומאה. Is עבודה זרה compared to a שרץ, which needs a כעדשה, or to a מת, which needs a כזית?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is the law regarding impurity? Since it is compared to a שרץ, maybe just as a שרץ makes things impure at a lentil-size, so too idolatry at a lentil-size. Or perhaps it is compared to a מת: just as a מת makes things impure at an olive-size, so too idolatry at an olive-size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא redefines the question: it is about טומאה, not the איסור. Then it lays out the two sides of the doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה is compared in פסוקים both to a שרץ and to a מת. If we follow the שרץ comparison, even a lentil-size idol makes things טמא. If we follow the מת comparison, it needs to be at least a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: it is compared (in the פסוק) to
a creeping animal that makes things טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the איסור. A tiny idol is fully forbidden. The question here is only about its טומאה.

phrases.english: Rather, regarding impurity — what (is the law)?
Since it is compared to a creeping animal:
just as a creeping animal (makes impure) at a lentil-bulk,
so too idolatry at a lentil-bulk.
Or perhaps, it is compared to a corpse:
just as a corpse (makes impure) at an olive-bulk,
so too idolatry at an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב יוסף by moving the question to טומאה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about the איסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about the minimum size for טומאה: a lentil (like a שרץ) or an olive (like a מת).

steps.title: A ברייתא resolves it: less than a כזית has no impurity
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that an idol smaller than a כזית has no טומאה at all, because a פסוק compares it to a מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא said, and some say it was רבה בר עולא: Come and hear what was taught: An idol smaller than an olive-bulk has no impurity at all, as it says, 'And he threw its dust on the graves of the common people.' Just as a מת makes things impure at an olive-size, so too an idol at an olive-size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אחדבוי's question with a ברייתא. A tiny idol under a כזית carries no טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the idol's dust being thrown on graves, which links עבודה זרה to a מת. So the size rule of a מת, a כזית, applies, and not the lentil-size rule of a שרץ.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (it was someone else)

steps.whatToRemember: For טומאה, עבודה זרה is compared to a מת, so it needs a כזית. An idol smaller than that has no טומאה at all, even though it is still fully forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one item can have different minimum sizes for different laws. Any size is enough for the איסור, but טומאה needs a כזית.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַוְיָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Avya said, and some say it was Rabba bar Ulla:
Come and hear, for it was taught:
Idolatry less than an olive-bulk
has no impurity at all,
as it is said:
"And he threw its dust
upon the graves of the common people" (II Kings 23:6) —
just as a corpse (makes impure) at an olive-bulk,
so too idolatry at an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the doubt laid out in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An idol smaller than a כזית has no טומאה, because it follows the rule of a מת.
steps.raayaObject: The minimum size for טומאה of עבודה זרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא based on מלכים ב כג:ו
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For טומאה, עבודה זרה needs a כזית, like a מת.

steps.title: What does each comparison teach according to רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law each comparison of עבודה זרה teaches according to רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבנן, for what law was it compared?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks what each of the three comparisons of עבודה זרה is meant to teach according to רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the פסוקים compared עבודה זרה to three things: a שרץ, a נדה, and a מת. According to רבנן, its טומאה works like a שרץ. So now we need to know what each comparison is actually for. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here the side that disagrees with רבי עקיבא
For what law? What practical rule does this teach?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis — for what law was it compared
phrases.notes: The question continues straight into the answer in the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the comparisons to שרץ and מת mentioned in Steps 11-12 and asks what all three comparisons accomplish.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical law taught by each of the three comparisons, according to רבנן.

steps.title: Each comparison teaches a leniency
steps.stepSummary: The comparison to שרץ teaches that it does not make things טמא by carrying. The comparison to נדה teaches that its separate pieces carry no טומאה. The comparison to מת teaches that a כעדשה-sized piece does not make things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: To a שרץ: it does not make things טמא by carrying. To a נדה: its separate pieces carry no טומאה. To a מת: it does not make things טמא with only a lentil's size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. Each of the three comparisons teaches a way in which the טומאה of עבודה זרה is lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like a שרץ, an idol does not make someone טמא just by carrying it (no טומאת משא). Like a נדה, whose separate limbs do not carry her טומאה, a broken-off piece of an idol does not carry טומאה. Like a מת, which needs a כזית, an idol does not make things טמא with only a כעדשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying, a way of becoming טמא even without touching
Limbs or body parts, here the broken-off pieces of an idol
The size of a lentil, the amount needed for טומאת שרץ

steps.confusionAlert: Each comparison is used for a different detail, so they do not contradict each other. עבודה זרה is like a שרץ for one law and like a מת for another.

phrases.english: To a creeping creature — that it does not make impure through carrying,
to a menstruant — that it has no impurity through separate limbs,
phrases.notes: רש"י reads all three comparisons as leniencies (כולהו לקולא), so here an idol's separate pieces carry no טומאה. Sefaria's translation reads this line differently.

phrases.english: to a corpse — that it does not make impure with a lentil's size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All three comparisons teach leniencies: no טומאת משא, no טומאה for separate pieces, and no טומאה for a כעדשה.

steps.title: Why not use the comparisons to be strict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe each comparison teaches a stringency instead. Like a שרץ, a כעדשה would make things טמא. Like a נדה, it would make things טמא through an אבן מסמא. Like a מת, it would make things טמא through an אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say they teach strictness: compared to a שרץ, to make things טמא with a lentil's size; to a נדה, to make things טמא through a heavy stone; to a מת, to make things טמא through a tent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the previous answer. Each comparison could just as easily teach a strict rule instead of a lenient one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every one of the three sources has both lenient and strict rules. So why did we pick only the lenient side of each? The challenge lists the matching stringency for each one: כעדשה for שרץ, אבן מסמא for נדה, and אהל for מת.

keyTerms.meaning: A very heavy stone resting on a טמא object; with a נדה, the things under it become טמא
A tent or roof; the טומאה of a מת spreads to everything under the same roof
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: Say instead it is for stringency:
for what law did the Torah compare it to a creeping creature —
to make impure with a lentil's size,
to a menstruant — to make impure through a heavy stone,
the Torah compared it to a corpse — to make impure through a tent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 14's choice to read each comparison as a leniency.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 14 that the comparisons teach only leniencies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A היקש could carry over either side of each source, so nothing forces us to choose the lenient side over the strict side.

steps.title: The impurity of idols is rabbinic, so we compare only to be lenient
steps.stepSummary: The טומאה of עבודה זרה is only דרבנן. For a rabbinic rule, we use a comparison to be lenient, never to be strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: The impurity of idols is rabbinic. When there is a choice between leniency and stringency, we compare for leniency and do not compare for stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Because the טומאה of idols is only rabbinic, the comparisons are used only for leniencies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, an idol does not carry טומאה at all; the פסוקים are only a hint (אסמכתא) for a rabbinic rule. Since the whole טומאה is rabbinic, the Sages did not extend it further. So when a comparison could go either way, it is applied only in the lenient direction.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבנן, the טומאה of עבודה זרה is rabbinic. Its comparisons to שרץ, נדה, and מת therefore teach only leniencies.

phrases.english: The impurity of idolatry is rabbinic,
and when there is a leniency and a stringency —
we compare for the leniency,
we do not compare for the stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle about how rabbinic rules are applied
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A היקש could teach either the strict or the lenient side of each source.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the טומאה is rabbinic, only the lenient side is carried over.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general approach: when a rabbinic rule is hinted at in a פסוק, the comparison is not pushed to create new stringencies.

steps.title: משנה: a ship cannot become impure
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a ship cannot become טמא, based on the פסוק 'דרך אניה בלב ים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: From where do we know that a ship is טהור? As it says: 'The way of a ship in the heart of the sea.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a ship cannot become טמא and brings a פסוק from משלי as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being טהור here means the ship cannot receive טומאה at all. The משנה does not yet explain how the פסוק proves this; the גמרא will explain it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure; here, unable to become טמא
A ship (the word used in the פסוק)

phrases.english: MISHNAH
From where do we know that a ship is pure —
as it is said: 'The way of a ship in the heart of the sea.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. Like the earlier משנה about עבודה זרה, it is a law hinted at by a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ship cannot become טמא, as hinted by 'דרך אניה בלב ים'.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that a ship is in the sea?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק says something so obvious: of course a ship is in the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It is obvious that a ship is in the heart of the sea!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the פסוק quoted in the משנה. It seems to tell us nothing new, so how can it teach any law?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes that a פסוק should not state something obvious. Pointing out the obvious wording opens the way to finding a hidden lesson in it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA
It is obvious — a ship is in the heart of the sea!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the proof-text of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק 'דרך אניה בלב ים' as a source for a law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words seem to describe something obvious, so they appear to teach nothing.

steps.title: A ship is like the sea
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק compares a ship to the sea: just as the sea is טהור, so is a ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us 'like the sea': just as the sea is טהור, so too a ship is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is not just describing where a ship sails. It is comparing the ship to the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a ship obviously sails in the sea, the extra words are read as a comparison. The sea can never become טמא, so the ship shares that status.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us — like the sea:

phrases.aramaic: מָה יָם טָהוֹר — אַף סְפִינָה טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.english: just as the sea is pure, so too a ship is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק as a comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק just describes the obvious fact that ships sail in the sea.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק compares a ship to the sea, which is טהור.

steps.title: חנניה learns it from a sack
steps.stepSummary: חנניה learns from a שק that only things carried both full and empty can become טמא. A ship cannot be carried when full, so it cannot become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא: חנניה says, we learn it from a sack. Just as a sack is carried full and empty, so too anything carried full and empty can become טמא. This excludes a ship, which is not carried when full.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a different source for the same law. חנניה learns it from the comparison to a שק instead of from the פסוק about the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists a שק together with wooden vessels that can become טמא. חנניה reads this as a rule: a vessel can become טמא only if it can be moved around both full and empty, like a sack. A ship is far too heavy to carry full, so it is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Carried around both full and empty

phrases.english: It was taught: Chananya says, let us learn it from a sack,
just as a sack is carried full and empty —
so too anything carried full and empty can become impure.
This excludes a ship, which is not carried when full.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same law taught in Steps 17-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel can become טמא only if it is carried both full and empty, like a sack, so a ship cannot.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two sources?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between learning from the sea and learning from the sack.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. Both sources say a ship is טהור, so it asks whether they ever lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two sources reach the same law, the גמרא looks for a case where they would rule differently. That case is given in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two sources from Steps 19 and 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where learning from 'בלב ים' and learning from שק give different results.

steps.title: The difference: an earthenware ship
steps.stepSummary: An earthenware ship is the difference. Learning from the sea, it is טהור because it is in the sea. Learning from the sack, the full-and-empty rule applies only to the materials listed with שק, so an earthenware ship can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is an earthenware ship. For the one who learns from 'a ship in the heart of the sea', this ship is also in the sea. For the one who learns from a sack, the rule applies only to the things written together with a sack: if they are carried full and empty, yes, and if not, no. But an earthenware ship can become טמא even though it is not carried full.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that an earthenware ship is where the two sources differ. Only the 'sea' source makes it טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the sea covers every ship, whatever it is made of. The sack rule only governs the materials listed with שק in the same פסוק (wood, cloth, leather, and sackcloth). Earthenware vessels have their own separate laws, so by the sack source an earthenware ship can become טמא even though it cannot be carried full.

keyTerms.meaning: Those materials written together with a sack in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Both sources agree that a wooden ship cannot become טמא. They differ about an earthenware ship: by the 'בלב ים' source it is טהור, and by חנניה's sack source it can become טמא.
steps.confusionAlert: The sack rule does not say that everything which cannot be carried full is טהור. It only applies to the materials listed together with a שק, and earthenware is not one of them.

phrases.english: The difference between them is an earthenware ship.
The one who says 'a ship in the heart of the sea' —
this one is also in the heart of the sea.
According to the one who says it is like a sack —
it applies only to those written together with a sack,
phrases.notes: ויקרא יא:לב lists עץ, בגד, עור, and שק.

phrases.english: so that if it is carried full and empty, yes, it becomes impure,
and if not — no.
But an earthenware ship can become impure

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵינָהּ מִיטַּלְטֶלֶת מְלֵאָה.
phrases.english: even though it is not carried when full.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An earthenware ship is טהור by the 'בלב ים' source but can become טמא by חנניה's sack source.

steps.title: A second difference: the Jordan River boat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another practical difference between the two sources. The case is a small Jordan River boat (ספינת הירדן). Learning from the sea, it is טהור. Learning from the sack, it can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, the difference is a Jordan boat. According to the one who learns from 'a ship in the midst of the sea', this is also a ship on the water, so it is טהור. According to the one who learns from 'carried full and empty', this boat is also carried full and empty, so it can become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question from Step 21 about what practical difference there is between the two sources. This time the case is a small boat used on the Jordan River.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources now give opposite results for the same boat. The 'sea' source looks only at where the boat is, and it is on water, so it stays טהור. The 'sack' source looks at how the boat is handled, and this small boat is carried around both loaded and empty, so it can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A small boat used on the Jordan River
According to the one who says
Carried around both full and empty

steps.confusionAlert: A river is not literally 'the sea'. But according to the 'sea' approach, any boat sitting on water counts as 'a ship in the midst of the sea', so the Jordan boat is טהור too.

phrases.english: Alternatively, there is a difference regarding a Jordan boat.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֳנִיָּה בְּלֶב יָם הִיא —
phrases.english: According to the one who says the source is 'a ship in the midst of the sea'
phrases.notes: This is the approach that learns from the sea, from Step 19.

phrases.aramaic: הָא נָמֵי אֳנִיָּה בְּלֶב יָם הִיא.
phrases.english: this is also a ship in the midst of the sea.
According to the one who says it depends on being carried full and empty
phrases.notes: This is חנניה's approach from the sack, from Step 20.

phrases.english: this is also carried both full and empty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question from Step 21, alongside the earthenware ship given in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference is there between learning from the sea and learning from the sack?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A Jordan boat: it is טהור according to the sea approach, and it can become טמא according to the sack approach.

steps.title: Why the Jordan boat can become טמא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן עקביא explains that a Jordan boat can become טמא because people load it on dry land and then lower it into the water. This shows that it is carried while full.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חנינא בן עקביא said: Why did they say a Jordan boat can become טמא? Because people load it on dry land and then lower it into the water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that backs up the claim from Step 23 that a Jordan boat is carried both full and empty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A big sea ship can never be carried while it is loaded. A small Jordan boat, however, is loaded on land and then moved into the river. That handling makes it like a sack, so it can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who explained the reason for the Jordan boat ruling

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chanina ben Akavya said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ סְפִינַת הַיַּרְדֵּן טְמֵאָה —
phrases.english: For what reason did they say that a Jordan boat can become impure?
Because they load it on dry land
and then lower it into the water.
phrases.notes: So it is moved while full, just like a sack.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim from Step 23 that a Jordan boat is carried full and empty.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a Jordan boat counts as carried both full and empty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא בן עקביא's explanation that it is loaded on land and then lowered into the water.

steps.title: Never miss even one moment of the study hall
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that a person should never stay away from the בית המדרש, even for one moment. The proof is that this משנה about the Jordan boat was learned for years without anyone knowing its reason, until רבי חנינא בן עקביא explained it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person should never keep himself away from the בית המדרש, even for one moment. This משנה was learned in the בית המדרש for many years, and its reason was not known until רבי חנינא בן עקביא came and explained it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the halacha to a lesson about Torah study. The lesson is drawn from the story behind רבי חנינא בן עקביא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the Jordan boat ruling stayed hidden for years. Someone who missed the moment רבי חנינא בן עקביא explained it would have missed that new understanding. Every moment in the בית המדרש could be the moment something new is revealed.

keyTerms.term: לְעוֹלָם אַל יִמְנַע אָדָם אֶת עַצְמוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A person should never hold himself back

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a technical halacha can teach a lasting lesson about being constantly present for Torah learning.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אַל יִמְנַע אָדָם אֶת עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: A person should never hold himself back
from the study hall, even for one moment,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי כַּמָּה שָׁנִים נִשְׁנֵית מִשְׁנָה זוֹ בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
phrases.english: for this mishna was taught for many years in the study hall
and its reason was not revealed

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁבָּא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא וּפֵירְשָׁהּ.
phrases.english: until Rabbi Chanina ben Akavya came and explained it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב לְעוֹלָם אַל יִמְנַע אָדָם אֶת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson about Torah study from רבי חנינא בן עקביא's explanation in Step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should never stay away from the בית המדרש, even for one moment.

steps.title: Learn Torah even at the moment of death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן adds that a person should not stop learning Torah even at the moment of death. He learns this from the verse 'This is the Torah: a person who dies in a tent'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said: A person should never keep himself away from the בית המדרש or from Torah, even at the moment of death. As it says, 'This is the Torah: a person who dies in a tent', which means that even when dying, one should be busy with Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching that goes even further than רב's teaching in Step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said not to miss even one moment. רבי יונתן says this applies even at the very end of life. He reads the verse as connecting 'Torah' with 'a person who dies'.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who teaches this lesson

keyTerms.term: זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל
keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the Torah: a person who dies in a tent' (במדבר יט:יד)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אַל יִמְנַע אָדָם אֶת עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: A person should never hold himself back
from the study hall and from words of Torah,
even at the moment of death,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל״ —
phrases.english: as it says: 'This is the Torah: a person who dies in a tent'

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָה תְּהֵא עוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: even at the moment of death, you should be busy with Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן לְעוֹלָם אַל יִמְנַע אָדָם אֶת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רב's teaching from Step 25 to include even the moment of death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should keep learning Torah even at the moment of death.

steps.title: Torah lasts only in someone who gives himself over to it
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the same verse differently: Torah stays only with someone who 'kills himself' over it, meaning he puts all his effort into it. This passage ends with רבא starting a new statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Words of Torah last only in someone who 'kills himself' over it, as it says, 'This is the Torah: a person who dies in a tent'. Then רבא said...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second reading of the same verse. At the end, it sets up the next teaching by introducing רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן read 'dies' literally, as the moment of death. ריש לקיש reads it as total devotion: a person must give up comfort and put everything into Torah for it to stay with him.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
'Kills himself' over it; devotes himself completely

steps.confusionAlert: 'Kills himself' does not mean literally ending his life. It means giving up comfort and pouring all his effort into Torah.
steps.whatToRemember: A Jordan boat is the second difference: it is טהור if we learn from the sea, and it can become טמא if we learn from the sack. Its reason, given by רבי חנינא בן עקביא, leads to lessons about never leaving the בית המדרש and devoting oneself fully to Torah.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Words of Torah do not endure
except in someone who kills himself over it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'This is the Torah: a person who dies in a tent.'
Rava said:
phrases.notes: This line introduces רבא's statement, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִתְקַיְּימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same verse used by רבי יונתן in Step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah endures only in someone who devotes himself completely to it.
